title: Capstone 1: A validated neural network from scratch
brief: Build, train and rigorously validate a two-layer neural network without autograd, then explain it and probe where it breaks. You are done only when every criterion has written evidence you would be comfortable defending to a reviewer.

criteria.text: Your backward pass equals both finite differences and PyTorch autograd.
criteria.evidence: Paste the maximum relative error from your gradient check and from the float64 PyTorch comparison (lesson 12 exercise). State the network sizes and batch used.

criteria.text: You can derive every gradient and every shape yourself.
criteria.evidence: Write the derivation of dW1, db1, dW2, db2 in your own words with shapes, as if teaching someone who knows only lessons 1-6.

criteria.text: You ran a controlled experiment on the learning rate (or width, or initialisation) and interpreted it.
criteria.evidence: Give a table of learning rates and final loss/accuracy over at least 3 seeds each, then explain what theory (lesson 7) predicts about the largest stable rate.

criteria.text: You found and explained a failure case.
criteria.evidence: Describe a setting where training fails (diverges, stalls at ln K, dead ReLUs...), what diagnostic exposed it, and the fix.

criteria.text: You can state the limits of your implementation.
criteria.evidence: List at least three things the from-scratch version does not do that a production framework does (e.g. numerical safeguards, performance, generality) and how you would test each.
